doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Gloria Lynne, Milt Hinton and later work
title: Electric bass and playing it left-handed
summary: May was pushed into electric bass, praises Bob Cranshaw's sound and jokes about Paul McCartney reversing strings.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I notice you started playing some electric bass.
I was kind of forced into that.
Yeah? Not something that you wanted to do?

If I could do it well, if I could please myself. The word on the grapevine was Bob Cranshaw and I had about the same kind of sound. I thought he had a really wonderful sound. He’s a really excellent playing string bass or — but that’s the only other compliment I ever got out of that. I don’t have the technique for that. So I’ve got to satisfy myself let’s say. I’d rather hear somebody else play that.
Plus you’d be playing it left handed.
Which makes — that I would have probably done. Because it’s easy to carry.
Yeah, that’s true. It’s that practical thing again.
